mainTopic: Sources that every ערוה counts from העראה, what the extra words נדה and העראה teach, and which half-relatives are forbidden
overview: The גמרא finishes rejecting an attempt to learn from נדה and אשת אח that every ערוה counts from the first stage of contact (העראה). Instead, רבי יונה brings a פסוק that compares all עריות to נדה. That leaves two words with no job. The word נדה written by אשת אח is used for רב הונא's teaching: a brother's wife is forbidden with כרת while her husband is alive, just as a נדה is forbidden with כרת until she becomes permitted. The extra העראה written by a father's sister and a mother's sister is moved over by רבא to teach that העראה counts even with a בהמה. A ברייתא then shows that the logic about these aunts can go either way, so a פסוק is needed to teach that they are forbidden through either parent. רבי אבהו explains why both aunts had to be written. רבא learns from the word דודו in the redemption laws that an uncle's wife is forbidden only through a paternal uncle. Finally, the גמרא quotes a משנה about a man who kept marrying his supposedly dead wife's sister, and the question about it comes on the next amud.

steps.title: What controls the status of נדה and אשת אח
steps.stepSummary: The status of נדה depends on days passing, and the status of אשת אח depends on whether there are children.
steps.simpleTranslation: With נדה, the matter depends on days. With a brother's wife, the תורה made it depend on children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the refutation from just before this. That refutation does not fit, because a נדה depends on days and an אשת אח depends on children, not on any person's lifetime. This sets up a better refutation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה stays forbidden for a set number of days, whether or not she keeps bleeding. An אשת אח stays forbidden or becomes permitted depending on whether her husband left children. In both cases, what ends the prohibition is something outside the person who caused it.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter depends on days
a woman forbidden because of her monthly period
a brother's wife, a forbidden relationship
'the Merciful One', meaning the תורה

phrases.english: The matter depends on days.
phrases.notes: This is about the נדה: her status runs by the count of days, not by whether she is still bleeding.

phrases.english: A brother's wife — the Merciful One made it depend on children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion that came just before this text, comparing נדה and אשת אח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies what really controls each prohibition
steps.terutzMaskana: נדה depends on days and אשת אח depends on children, which are outside factors.

steps.title: Why נדה and אשת אח cannot teach about אשת איש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows a difference: whoever forbids an אשת איש can also permit her, which is not true of נדה and אשת אח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, refute it this way: נדה and אשת אח are special, because what forbids them does not permit them. Can you say the same about an אשת איש, where the one who forbids her can also permit her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a stronger reason why you cannot learn all עריות from נדה and אשת אח together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband makes his wife forbidden to everyone else, and he can also make her permitted by giving her a גט. A נדה or an אשת אח becomes permitted only through outside factors, such as time or the husband's death. Because of this difference, the two cases cannot serve as a model for אשת איש.

keyTerms.meaning: refutes, attacks a derivation
the one who forbids them is the one who permits them
a married woman
'what about X, which is special because...', the standard way to break a comparison

phrases.english: Rather, refute it like this:
What about a נדה and a brother's wife
which are special in that what forbids them does not permit them.
Will you say the same about a married woman,
where the one who forbids her permits her!
phrases.notes: The husband forbids her to others by marrying her, and permits her by divorcing her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier way of refuting with a sharper one.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning that all עריות count from העראה by comparing to נדה and אשת אח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשת איש has a feature those two lack: the one who forbids her can also permit her.

steps.title: A פסוק groups all עריות together with נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה (or רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) brings a פסוק that compares all עריות to נדה, so all of them work through העראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יונה said (some say it was רב הונא son of רב יהושע): the פסוק says, 'For whoever does any of these abominations, the souls that do them will be cut off.' All the עריות are compared to נדה. Just as נדה counts from the first stage of contact, so do all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The comparison approach failed, so the גמרא brings a new source. A single פסוק covers all the עריות at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing פסוק of the chapter on עריות speaks about all of them together. That links every ערוה to נדה, which appears in that chapter. Since נדה counts from העראה, every ערוה does too, and no comparison is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: comparison made by the פסוק itself; 'they were compared'
the very first stage of contact in relations
the forbidden relationships

steps.whatToRemember: All עריות count from the first stage of contact, because the פסוק compares them all to נדה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a forbidden relationship is already violated at the first stage of contact, for every ערוה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yona said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
the verse says:
"For whoever shall do
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29

phrases.english: any of these abominations,
the souls that do them shall be cut off" —
all the forbidden relations are compared to a נדה:
just as a נדה is with the initial stage,
so too all are with the initial stage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new source after the comparison was refuted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 18:29, which compares all עריות to נדה

steps.title: Then why is נדה written by אשת אח?
steps.stepSummary: If all עריות are already compared to נדה, the word נדה written in the פסוק about אשת אח seems unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'נדה' that is written about a brother's wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source by pointing to a word that now seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the word נדה by אשת אח was used to teach העראה for אשת אח. Now the general פסוק already teaches that for every ערוה. So the word must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (asking about an extra word)
regarding, written next to

phrases.english: But then, the word "נדה" that is written
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:21, which says about a brother's wife, נִדָּה הִוא.

phrases.english: regarding a brother's wife, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא ״נִדָּה״ דִּכְתִיבָא גַּבֵּי אֵשֶׁת אָח לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 3 by asking what an extra word is for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word נדה in the פסוק about אשת אח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the general פסוק covers העראה for all עריות, this word has no job left.

steps.title: The word is used for רב הונא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The word נדה by אשת אח is needed for רב הונא's teaching about a hint for יבמה in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what רב הונא said. רב הונא said: where in the תורה is there a hint for a יבמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word נדה has a different job and brings רב הונא's statement. This also sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is not wasted. It teaches something about a יבמה, which רב הונא calls a 'רמז', a hint. As first quoted, though, his question sounds strange.

keyTerms.meaning: for that which רב הונא taught
a hint in the פסוק
a widow whose husband died without children, waiting for his brother
from where (do we know)?

phrases.english: For that which Rav Huna taught.
As Rav Huna said:
From where in the Torah is there a hint to a yevama?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by giving the word a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new job
steps.terutzMaskana: The word נדה by אשת אח is used for רב הונא's teaching about יבמה.

steps.title: But יבום is written openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: why look for a hint about יבמה when the תורה says it openly?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where?! It is written: 'Her brother-in-law shall come to her'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רב הונא's question was worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of יבום is stated clearly in the תורה. So asking for a mere 'hint' about a יבמה makes no sense, and his question must mean something more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written!
her brother-in-law shall come to her (the command of יבום)

phrases.english: From where?!
But it is written: "Her brother-in-law shall come to her"!
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב הונא's statement from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's question 'where is the hint for a יבמה?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יבום is stated openly in a פסוק, so there is no need for a hint.

steps.title: What רב הונא really asked
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא meant: where is the hint that a יבמה is forbidden to the brother while her husband is alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: where is the hint that a יבמה is forbidden during her husband's lifetime?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rephrases רב הונא's question so it makes sense. Step 8 then asks whether a source is needed at all, step 9 rejects that challenge, and the source comes in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about the מצוה of יבום itself. It is about the woman's status before she becomes a יבמה. While her husband is alive, even if he divorced her, she is forbidden to his brother. רב הונא wants to know where the תורה hints at that, and the word נדה will be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: during her husband's lifetime
forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The word נדה by אשת אח is kept for רב הונא's hint that a יבמה is forbidden to the brother while her husband is alive.

phrases.english: Rather: a hint to a yevama
that she is forbidden in her husband's lifetime, from where?
phrases.notes: Forbidden to the brother, even if her husband divorced her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רֶמֶז לִיבָמָה שֶׁאֲסוּרָה בְּחַיֵּי בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by restating רב הונא's question more precisely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא was asking for a source for יבום itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking for a hint that a יבמה is forbidden to the brother while her husband lives.

steps.title: Why do we need a hint? Logic already tells us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: no hint is needed, because if the תורה permits the יבמה after her husband dies, she must be forbidden while he is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is just logic! The תורה says she is permitted after her husband dies. That shows she is forbidden while he is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's question. It says we don't need a hint in the תורה, because plain logic already shows that a brother's wife is forbidden while her husband is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lets the brother marry the יבמה only 'after her husband's death.' If he was allowed to marry her anyway, there would be no point in saying 'after.' So the prohibition during the husband's life seems to come straight from the wording, with no hint needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning; something you know from thinking it through, not from a פסוק
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
She is permitted
By implication; from the fact that

phrases.english: This is a matter of logic!
From the fact that the Merciful One said
that after her husband's death she is permitted,
phrases.notes: This refers to the מצוה of יבום, which applies only once the husband has died.

phrases.english: it is implied that during her husband's lifetime she is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the hint that רב הונא was looking for in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's search for a hint that a יבמה is forbidden during her husband's lifetime
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permission 'after death' already implies that she is forbidden before death, so no hint is needed.

steps.title: Logic alone does not prove the prohibition is כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the logic. Maybe during the husband's life marrying her is just optional. Or maybe it is forbidden only as a weak prohibition that comes from a positive command, with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe after the husband dies marrying her is a מצוה, and while he is alive it is just optional? Or maybe after he dies, yes, it is allowed, and while he is alive, no, it is not allowed. But a prohibition that we only learn from a positive command counts only as a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the logic from the last step. It shows that the words 'after her husband's death' do not prove a serious prohibition while he is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the word 'after' may only mean that after death it becomes a מצוה, while before death it is just allowed (רשות). Option two: even if it is forbidden before death, a prohibition learned only by implication from a positive command (a לאו הבא מכלל עשה) has the weight of an עשה. It would not be a real לאו, and certainly not כרת. So we still need a פסוק to show that the prohibition is כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (used to show that a proof is not certain)
A commandment, something you are obligated to do
Optional; allowed but not required
Alternatively; or else
A prohibition that comes only by implication from a positive command; it counts as a positive command, not a full prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: The second option does agree that she is forbidden while her husband is alive. The question is only how serious that prohibition is: a weak עשה-level prohibition, or full כרת.

phrases.english: But perhaps after her husband's death it is a מצוה,
while during her husband's lifetime it is optional?

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: לְאַחַר מִיתַת בַּעְלָהּ אִין,
phrases.english: Or alternatively: after her husband's death, yes, she is permitted,
during her husband's lifetime, no, she is not permitted,
but a prohibition that comes by implication from a positive command has the status of a positive command,
phrases.notes: In other words, that would make it only a light prohibition, with no כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 8's claim that logic alone is enough.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference from 'after her husband's death' to a serious prohibition during his lifetime
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference could mean only 'optional versus מצוה,' or at most a weak עשה-level prohibition. It does not prove כרת.

steps.title: The פסוק calls a brother's wife נדה to teach כרת
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls a brother's wife נדה. This teaches that just as a נדה, who later becomes permitted, is forbidden with כרת in the meantime, so too a brother's wife is forbidden with כרת while her husband is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And a man who takes his brother's wife, it is נדה.' Is his brother's wife really a נדה? Rather, she is like a נדה. A נדה becomes permitted later, but while she is forbidden it is כרת. So too a brother's wife: even though she can become permitted later, while her husband is alive it is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the hint רב הונא was looking for. The word נדה in the פסוק about a brother's wife teaches that she is forbidden with כרת while her husband is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother's wife is obviously not always a נדה, so the word must be a comparison. A נדה is a case of a woman who will later become permitted but is forbidden with כרת for now. A brother's wife is the same: she may later become permitted through יבום, but during her husband's lifetime she is forbidden with כרת. This answers both weak options from Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it really...? (asked with surprise)
Permission; a stage when something becomes allowed
Spiritual cutting off, the תורה's punishment for the most serious forbidden relationships

steps.whatToRemember: The word נדה by אשת אח is used for רב הונא's teaching. A brother's wife, like a נדה, may become permitted later, but until then she is forbidden with כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the word נדה by אשת אח was still needed, even though Step 3 compared all עריות to נדה. It is needed for this specific teaching about כרת during the husband's lifetime.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And a man who takes
his brother's wife, it is נדה'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:21

phrases.english: But is his brother's wife a menstruating woman?
Rather, she is like a menstruating woman:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נִדָּה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ
phrases.english: Just as a menstruating woman, even though she has
a permitted stage afterward,
at the time she is forbidden, it is with כרת,
so too a brother's wife [as well],
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets; it just means 'too'.

phrases.english: even though she has
a permitted stage afterward,
during her husband's lifetime it is with כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִקַּח אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו נִדָּה הִיא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 9 showed that logic is not enough, this step gives the פסוק that proves the prohibition is כרת.
steps.raayaObject: A יבמה is forbidden with כרת to her husband's brother during her husband's lifetime
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 20:21, 'אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו נִדָּה הִיא': the brother's wife is compared to a נדה

steps.title: Then why is העראה written by the aunts?
steps.stepSummary: If all עריות learn העראה from נדה, why does the תורה write העראה again by a father's sister and a mother's sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the העראה that is written about a father's sister and a mother's sister, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier idea from Step 3 and raises a new question about it. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 taught that all עריות are compared to נדה, so העראה (the first stage of relations) counts for all of them. If so, the separate mention of העראה in the פסוק about a father's sister and a mother's sister seems unneeded. The גמרא now asks what that extra mention comes to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The first stage of relations, which counts as full relations for punishment
A father's sister (an aunt)
Why do I need it? (asking what an extra source adds)

phrases.english: But then, the העראה that is written
phrases.notes: This is the word 'הֶעֱרָה' in ויקרא 20:19.

phrases.english: regarding a father's sister and a mother's sister,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַעֲרָאָה דִּכְתִיבָא גַּבֵּי אָחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם, לְמָה לִּי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the word נדה by אשת אח has been explained, the גמרא returns to the derivation in Step 3 and challenges it from a different angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in Step 3 that all עריות learn העראה from the comparison to נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If העראה is already learned for all עריות from נדה, then writing it again by the father's and mother's sister is redundant.

steps.title: The extra word is needed for רבינא's question about a male
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra word העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister is needed to answer רבינא's question to רבא about העראה with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what רבינא asked רבא: one who does העראה with a male, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer step 11's question. It suggests the extra העראה is needed to settle רבינא's question about a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked why the תורה repeats העראה if all עריות already learn it from נדה. This step suggests the extra word is not wasted. It would teach that העראה counts as a forbidden act with a male (משכב זכור).

keyTerms.meaning: One who does העראה, the first, partial stage of relations
A male (this is about the איסור of משכב זכור)
He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)

phrases.english: It is needed for what רבינא asked of רבא:
phrases.notes: "It" means the extra word העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister, from step 11.

phrases.english: One who does העראה with a male, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to step 11's question about the extra העראה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister seems useless, since all עריות learn it from נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is needed to answer רבינא's question about a male (this is rejected right away in the next step).

steps.title: No question about a male, since the פסוק compares him to a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The פסוק about a male says "משכבי אשה," so whatever counts with a woman, including העראה, already counts with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a male? It is written "the lyings of a woman"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down step 12. There is nothing to ask about a male, so the extra word cannot be needed for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says not to lie with a male "as with a woman." That ties the two together, so העראה counts with a male just as it does with a woman. The extra word is still left without a job.

keyTerms.meaning: The lyings of a woman: the פסוק's way of comparing a male to a woman
It is written (in the פסוק)

phrases.english: About a male? "The lyings of a woman" is written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 12's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the extra word is about a male
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The law for a male already comes from "משכבי אשה," so the question was never open.

steps.title: Rather, רבינא's question was about a בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects itself. רבינא's real question was about העראה with a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one who does העראה with an animal, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says "rather" and changes the question. The extra word is needed for the case of a בהמה, and this sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male is covered by "משכבי אשה," but nothing compares a בהמה to a woman. So it is a real question whether העראה counts as a forbidden act with a בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: it signals a corrected version
An animal (this is about the איסור of רביעת בהמה)

phrases.english: Rather: one who does העראה with an animal, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected male case with the case of a בהמה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of רבינא's question
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא asked about a בהמה, which has no פסוק comparing it to a woman.

steps.title: רבא: move the extra word over to teach בהמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the extra העראה is not needed for its own place, because a father's sister and a mother's sister already learn it through the הקש of רבי יונה. So we apply it to a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is not needed for העראה where it is written, by a father's sister and a mother's sister, since that comes from the הקש of רבי יונה, apply it to העראה with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבינא. The extra word teaches that העראה counts as a forbidden act even with a בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule "אם אינו ענין": if a word is not needed in its own place, it teaches something somewhere else. A father's sister and a mother's sister already get העראה from the הקש to נדה, so this word is free to teach about בהמה. This also answers step 11's question.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic, move it to teach a different one
Apply it to a different topic
A comparison the תורה makes by putting two things together

steps.whatToRemember: The extra העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister teaches that העראה counts as a forbidden act even with a בהמה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering רבינא.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for העראה

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיבָא גַּבֵּי אֲחוֹת אָב וַאֲחוֹת אֵם,

since that comes from the comparison of רבי יונה,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does העראה with a בהמה count as a forbidden act?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The extra העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister is moved over to teach בהמה.

steps.title: Why teach בהמה from a כרת case and not a court-death case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a בהמה is punished with court death. Why would the תורה write its העראה rule by sins that only get כרת? It should be written by a court-death sin, so one court-death case learns from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a בהמה is among those punished with court death, why is its העראה written by those punished with כרת? Let it be written by a court-death case, and we would learn court death from court death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. The source seems to be in the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's sister and a mother's sister are כרת sins, while a בהמה gets court death. It is more natural to learn a law from a similar kind of case. So if the תורה wanted to teach about בהמה, why put the hint among the כרת sins?

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all: it opens a challenge based on known facts
Sins punished with death by the court
Sins punished with כרת
And let us learn (one case from another)

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי בְּהֵמָה חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין הִיא,
phrases.english: Since a בהמה is among those punished with court death,
why is its העראה written
by those punished with כרת?
Let it be written by a court-death case,

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵילַף מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין מִמִּיתַת בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: and we would learn court death from court death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges where רבא's source is placed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's teaching that the extra העראה by a father's sister and a mother's sister is about a בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A court-death law should be hinted among court-death sins, not among כרת sins.

steps.title: The whole פסוק is there to teach, so this part teaches too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the whole פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister is written to teach extra lessons. So this word is also written there to teach one, the lesson about a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the entire פסוק comes to be expounded, this matter is also written in it to be expounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16. The hint is placed in that פסוק because that פסוק is full of lessons anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why a בהמה law sits among כרת sins. The answer is that this particular פסוק is written mainly to teach other things. So the תורה added this lesson there too, even though it belongs to a different kind of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, as long as (one thing came along with another)
To be expounded, to teach an extra lesson
The פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The hint about בהמה is in the פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister because that whole פסוק is written to teach extra lessons.

phrases.english: Since the entire פסוק comes to be expounded,
phrases.notes: The פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister (ויקרא 20:19).

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ נָמֵי הָא מִילְּתָא לִדְרָשָׁא.
phrases.english: this matter is also written in it to be expounded.

steps.terutzMaskana: That פסוק is entirely written to teach lessons, so this lesson was added there as well.

steps.title: What extra lesson does the פסוק teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra lesson is in the פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the extra lesson?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: it wants to know which lesson the פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister comes to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the גמרא said the whole פסוק is written to teach extra lessons. Now it asks for the main lesson, the one the פסוק is mostly there for. The answer comes from a ברייתא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
An extra lesson learned from a פסוק

phrases.english: What is the exposition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the extra lesson from Step 17 actually is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra lesson the פסוק of a father's sister and a mother's sister teaches.

steps.title: A father's sister from either side is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a father's sister is forbidden whether she is his sister from the father's side or the mother's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Do not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister." This means she is forbidden whether she is his sister from the father or from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: the lesson is that a father's sister is forbidden even if she is only a half-sister of the father, from either parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your father's sister might share both of his parents, only his father, or only his mother. The ברייתא says every one of these counts. This is the extra lesson the פסוק teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Your father's sister

keyTerms.term: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם
keyTerms.meaning: Whether from the father or from the mother

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:12

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב, בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother.
phrases.notes: She is your father's sister either through his father or through his mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra lesson is that a father's sister is forbidden whether she is his sister from the father's side or from the mother's side.

steps.title: Maybe only a sister from the father's side counts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether perhaps only a father's sister from the father's side is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say from the father or from the mother? Or maybe it is only from the father and not from the mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own rule. Maybe only a half-sister through the father counts, and not one through the mother. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא wants to show that the rule needs a reason and is not simply obvious. It raises the narrower option so it can weigh the two sides in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say...? (opens a question in a ברייתא)
Or is it only...?

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: Do you say whether from the father or from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם —
phrases.english: or is it only from the father and not from the mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how wide the rule from Step 19 is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a father's sister from the mother's side is also forbidden, or only one from the father's side.

steps.title: Compare her to one's own sister
steps.stepSummary: Logic suggests a comparison to one's own sister, who is forbidden from either parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be learned by logic. He is punished here, and he is punished for his sister. Just as his sister is forbidden whether from the father or the mother, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to prove the wide rule by logic: it compares a father's sister to one's own sister, who is forbidden whether she shares his father or his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases carry punishment, so the ברייתא wants them to follow the same pattern. Since a half-sister from either parent is forbidden, a father's half-sister from either parent should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be learned by logic
Punished; liable
His own sister

phrases.english: And it is logical:
he is liable here and he is liable with his sister,

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲחוֹתוֹ — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: just as with his sister, whether from the father or from the mother,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: so too here, whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical proof for the wide option raised in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That a father's sister is forbidden from either side.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to one's own sister, who is forbidden from either parent.

steps.title: Or compare her to one's uncle's wife
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different comparison: to one's uncle's wife, where only a brother from the father counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: he is punished here, and he is punished for his uncle's wife. Just as with his uncle's wife it is only from the father and not from the mother, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the proof. Maybe a father's sister should be compared to one's uncle's wife, where the rule is narrower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An uncle's wife is forbidden only if the uncle is the father's brother through the father, not only through the mother. If a father's sister follows that pattern, she would be forbidden only from the father's side. So the comparison to a sister is no longer certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way (offer a different comparison)
His uncle's wife, the wife of his father's brother

steps.confusionAlert: Here דודתו is not a blood aunt. It means the wife of his father's brother, a relative only by marriage.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
he is liable here and he is liable with his aunt,

phrases.aramaic: מָה דּוֹדָתוֹ — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: just as with his aunt, from the father and not from the mother,
phrases.notes: She is forbidden only if her husband is the father's brother through the father, not only through the mother.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן — מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: so too here, from the father and not from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of Step 21 by offering a competing one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Weakens the proof from one's own sister by offering an equally possible comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a second case, the uncle's wife, that is also punished but follows a narrower rule.

steps.title: Arguing that a sister is the better comparison
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that a sister is the better comparison, since both are relatives by birth, while an uncle's wife is related only by marriage. The next step challenges this argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which it is more like. We learn a prohibition that comes by itself from a prohibition that comes by itself. The uncle's wife is no proof, since hers is not a prohibition that comes by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to break the tie between the two comparisons. It argues that a father's sister is more like one's own sister, so she would be forbidden from either side. The next step pushes back on this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister and a father's sister are forbidden because of birth. Nobody had to marry anyone for the איסור to exist (איסור הבא מאליו). An uncle's wife is forbidden only because she married the uncle, so she is a weaker match and cannot be used to prove the narrow rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which it is more like
We learn (one case from another)
A prohibition that comes by itself, through birth and not marriage
And do not bring a proof from...

steps.whatToRemember: This attempt to pick the closer comparison does not hold up. The next step offers an equally good grouping, which is why the ברייתא ends up needing a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move, 'נראה למי דומה', for weighing two comparisons. Here, though, it is countered right away.

phrases.english: Let us see to which it is similar.
We derive a prohibition that comes on its own
from a prohibition that comes on its own,
phrases.notes: Both a sister and a father's sister are forbidden through birth, with no marriage needed.

phrases.english: and his aunt cannot prove otherwise,
since it is not a prohibition that comes on its own.
phrases.notes: She becomes forbidden only by marrying the uncle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 22's comparison to the uncle's wife and argues for the sister comparison of step 21. Step 24 then challenges this.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This proposed logic, that a father's sister is more like one's own sister, is countered in the next step. The final source is the פסוק.

steps.title: Pushing back: maybe compare to the uncle's wife after all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on its own conclusion. Maybe a father's sister should be compared to the uncle's wife, since both are 'father's relatives'. The sister case does not disprove this, because a sister is his own relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: we should learn about the father's relatives (the father's sister) from the father's relatives (the father's brother's wife). His own sister cannot prove otherwise, because she is his own direct relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the comparison it just chose in step 23. It offers a different way to group the cases, which would lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, the sister won because she and the father's sister are both blood relatives. Now the ברייתא groups the cases another way. The father's sister and the uncle's wife both come to him through his father, while his own sister is his own relative and not a 'father's relative'. With two equally good comparisons pulling in opposite directions, logic alone cannot settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way: a formula that offers a different line of reasoning
We derive or learn one case from another
Prove or show otherwise
His own relatives, related to him directly and not through his father

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not reach a final answer. It only shows that the logic can go either way. That is exactly why the next step needs a פסוק.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
we derive the father's relatives from the father's relatives,
phrases.notes: He means: learn the father's sister from the father's brother's wife, since both come through the father.

phrases.english: and do not let his sister prove otherwise,
since she is his own relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 23 by offering an opposite grouping of the cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the comparison to one's sister settles the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sister is his own relative, while the father's sister and the uncle's wife are both father's relatives. So the uncle's wife may be the closer match.

steps.title: The verse teaches: forbidden from either parent
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot decide, the ברייתא brings the פסוקים. A father's sister and a mother's sister are both forbidden, whether they share the father or the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: 'The nakedness of your father's sister you shall not uncover', whether from the father or from the mother. And: 'The nakedness of your mother's sister you shall not uncover', whether from the father or from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא settles the question with a פסוק instead of logic. Both aunts are forbidden even if they are only half-sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 21 to 24 showed that reasoning could point both ways. The phrase תלמוד לומר signals that the תורה itself decides. The rule now covers both the father's sister and the mother's sister, through either parent.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says: introduces a פסוק as the deciding source
A forbidden relationship

keyTerms.term: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם
keyTerms.meaning: Whether from the father or from the mother, meaning a full or half sibling on either side

steps.whatToRemember: A father's sister and a mother's sister are both forbidden, even if they are only half-sisters of the parent through either the father or the mother. This comes from the פסוק, not from logic.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says:
'The nakedness of your father's sister you shall not uncover'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:12

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother.
'The nakedness of your mother's sister you shall not uncover'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:13

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאָב בֵּין מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: whether from the father or from the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock from step 24 by turning to the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both a father's sister and a mother's sister are forbidden through either parent, based on the פסוקים.

steps.title: Why write both the father's sister and the mother's sister?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה needed two separate פסוקים, one for the father's sister and one for the mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the תורה to write this about a father's sister, and why do I need it written about a mother's sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why there are two separate פסוקים. This question sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. If one aunt could be learned from the other, one of the פסוקים would seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about a seemingly extra source
To write, meaning for the Torah to state it

phrases.english: Why do I need it written about a father's sister,
why do I need it written about a mother's sister?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two פסוקים quoted in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why couldn't one aunt be learned from the other, which would make one פסוק unnecessary?

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the father's sister shares the family line
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says both פסוקים are needed. If only the father's sister were written, we would say she is special because family lineage follows the father, and the mother's sister would not be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: both are necessary. If the תורה had written only about a father's sister, we would say that is because she shares his family line. But a mother's sister, I would say, is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו starts answering by showing why the father's sister alone would not teach us about the mother's sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Family lineage (חייס) goes through the father, so the father's sister belongs to his family line in a way the mother's sister does not. That special feature means we could not extend her prohibition to the mother's sister.

keyTerms.meaning: They are necessary: both sources are needed
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Family lineage or line, which follows the father
I would say not

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: both are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written it only about a father's sister,
that is because she shares his family line,
but a mother's sister, I would say, is not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's sister has a special feature, shared lineage, so the mother's sister could not be learned from her.

steps.title: The mother's sister is certainly related, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If only the mother's sister were written, we would say she is special because the relationship to one's mother is certain. The father's sister would not be included, so both פסוקים are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only about a mother's sister, we would say that is because she is certainly his relative. But a father's sister, I would say, is not forbidden. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו finishes his answer by showing the opposite direction. Each aunt has her own special feature, so the Torah had to write both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who a person's mother is can be known for certain, while who his father is cannot be known with the same certainty. So the mother's sister has an advantage the father's sister lacks. Since each case has an edge the other does not, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: She is certain: the relationship through the mother is definite
It is necessary: the closing word of a 'both are needed' explanation

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה wrote both aunts because each has her own advantage. The father's sister shares the family line, and the mother's sister is certainly related.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written it only about a mother's sister,
that is because she is certainly his relative,
phrases.notes: Who your mother is can be known for sure, but who your father is cannot be known with the same certainty.

phrases.english: but a father's sister, I would say, is not forbidden;
so it is necessary to write both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבהו's answer with the reverse direction and concludes that both פסוקים are needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mother's sister has a special feature, a certain relationship, so the father's sister could not be learned from her. Therefore both פסוקים are needed.

steps.title: Where do we know the uncle's wife is only from the father's side?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's assumption that דודתו is forbidden only when the uncle is the father's brother from the same father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for his aunt, the uncle's wife, the תנא took it as obvious that this means an uncle from the father and not from the mother. Where does he learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: Until now the גמרא explained why the Torah wrote both the father's sister and the mother's sister. Now it turns to the uncle's wife and asks what the source is for the תנא's assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the aunts, the ברייתא said both sides of the family are forbidden. With דודתו, the תנא simply assumed that only the father's brother through the same father counts. The גמרא wants to know what this assumption is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: His aunt by marriage: the wife of his uncle
It is obvious to him; he takes it for granted
From the father and not from the mother
From where does he know this?

steps.confusionAlert: Here דודתו is not a blood aunt. It is the wife of his uncle. 'From the father' means the uncle is his father's brother through the same father, not only through the same mother.

phrases.english: And his aunt, where it is obvious to the תנא
phrases.notes: דודתו here means his uncle's wife, not his father's or mother's sister.

phrases.english: that it is from the father and not from the mother,
from where does he know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדוֹדָתוֹ, דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּמִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two aunts (blood relatives) to the uncle's wife, where the ברייתא made a different assumption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the prohibition of the uncle's wife applies only to a paternal uncle.

steps.title: רבא learns it from the word 'his uncle' in the redemption laws
steps.stepSummary: רבא uses a גזירה שוה. The word דודו appears both in the forbidden-relations פסוק and in the פסוק about redeeming a relative. In the redemption law it means a paternal uncle, so it means the same thing here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we learn it from 'his uncle' and 'his uncle'. Here it is written, 'he has uncovered his uncle's nakedness', and there it is written, 'either his uncle or his uncle's son shall redeem him'. Just as there it is from the father and not from the mother, so too here it is from the father and not from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He links the uncle in the עריות פסוק to the uncle in the redemption פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה lets us carry the meaning of a word from one place in the תורה to another. In the laws of גאולה, 'his uncle' means a relative on the father's side. So in the עריות פסוק, 'his uncle' also means the father's side only.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from; it is learned from (a גזירה שוה)
Learning from a shared word in two פסוקים
He shall redeem him
Just as there, so too here

It is learned from "his uncle" and "his uncle".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of דודו from the redemption laws, where 'uncle' means the father's side only.

steps.title: How do we know the redemption law is only on the father's side?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that in the laws of גאולה, 'his uncle' means only the father's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, in the redemption law, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's proof depends on the redemption law being about the father's side only. Now the גמרא asks for the source of that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה only works if the meaning in the source פסוק is clear. So the גמרא checks the foundation: why is the uncle in the redemption פסוק only a paternal relative?

keyTerms.meaning: And there (in the other case)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the redemption פסוק that רבא just used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the source that רבא's גזירה שוה relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that redemption by an uncle applies only to the father's side.

steps.title: Only the father's side is called 'family'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ממשפחתו יגאלנו, 'of his family shall redeem him'. Only the father's family is called 'family', not the mother's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Of his family shall redeem him.' The father's family is called family. The mother's family is not called family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the word 'family' in the same redemption פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The redemption פסוק says the redeemer must be 'of his family'. Since family lineage follows the father, only the father's relatives count. This makes the redemption meaning clear, and through the גזירה שוה the uncle's wife is limited to a paternal uncle.

keyTerms.meaning: From his family
The father's family is called 'family'

steps.whatToRemember: The chain is: דודתו is a paternal uncle's wife, because דודו is learned from the redemption פסוק, and there 'his family' means only the father's side.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Of his family shall redeem him",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:49

phrases.english: the father's family is called family,
the mother's family is not called family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 and completes רבא's derivation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ממשפחתו shows that only the father's relatives count, because only the father's family is called 'family'.

steps.title: A new משנה: the man who kept marrying his wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה. A man was told his wife died, so he married her sister. This happened again and again, alternating between paternal and maternal sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which we learned in a משנה: They told him, 'Your wife died,' and he married her sister from her father. She died, and he married her sister from her mother. She died, and he married her sister from her father. She died, and he married her sister from her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by quoting a משנה. The quote continues in steps 34 and 35, and the גמרא's question about it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new wife is a sister of the one before. But they alternate: one shares the father, the next shares the mother. This makes some of the women related to each other and some not, and it opens a discussion of which marriages take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which we learned in a משנה
Your wife died
Her sister through her father
Her sister through her mother

steps.confusionAlert: Each sister is related only to the woman right before her. Wife #3 shares a mother with wife #2, but she may not be related at all to wife #1.

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a משנה:
They said to him: Your wife died,
and he married her sister from her father,
she died, and he married her sister from her mother,
phrases.notes: 'Her' now means the second wife. Each new wife is the sister of the wife just before.

phrases.english: she died, and he married her sister from her father,
she died, and he married her sister from her mother —

steps.title: Wives one, three, and five are valid; two and four are not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the first, third, and fifth women are valid wives who free their צרות. The second and fourth are forbidden as אחות אשה, so their marriages do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is permitted to the first, third, and fifth women, and they free their co-wives. He is forbidden to the second and fourth, and if one of them does יבום, it does not free her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it began in step 33 and now reaches its ruling: which of the five women are real wives and which are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All five women are actually alive. Wife 2 is the paternal sister of wife 1, and wife 4 is the paternal sister of wife 3, so each is אחות אשה of a living wife and her marriage is void. Wives 1, 3, and 5 are not sisters of one another, so their marriages are valid. Because of this, only they count as real wives for the laws of יבום and צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted. Here it means the marriage is valid.
Forbidden. Here it means the marriage does not take effect.
A co-wife, meaning another wife of the same husband. צָרוֹתֵיהֶן means 'their co-wives'.
Exempts, or frees. When one widow does יבום or חליצה, the other widows are freed.
Intercourse. Here it means the act of יבום done with the dead husband's brother.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count every second wife as forbidden. Each woman is the sister of only the woman right before her, alternating between father's side and mother's side. So wife 3 is not related to wife 1, and wife 5 is not related to wife 3.

phrases.english: He is permitted to the first
and to the third and to the fifth,
phrases.notes: These three are not sisters of one another, so his marriages to them are real.

phrases.english: and they free their co-wives.
And he is forbidden to the second and to the fourth,
and the intercourse of one of them
phrases.notes: If this man dies childless and one of these women does יבום with his brother.

phrases.english: does not free her co-wife.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (continuation of the quoted משנה from step 33)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quote begun in step 33 by giving its ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wives 1, 3, and 5 are valid and free their צרות. Wives 2 and 4 are void as אחות אשה, so their יבום does not free a צרה.

steps.title: If the first wife really died, the valid wives flip
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a second case. If the first wife truly died before he married the second, then wives 2 and 4 are valid, and wives 3 and 5 are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married the second only after the first had died, he is permitted to the second and fourth, and they free their co-wives. He is forbidden to the third and fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second version of the same story, where the report about the first wife was true, and shows how that changes every later marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once wife 1 is really dead, wife 2 is no longer the sister of a living wife, so her marriage is valid. That makes wife 3 the sister of a living wife (wife 2), so her marriage is void. Wife 4 is related only to wife 3, who was never a real wife, so wife 4 is valid. Wife 5 is then the sister of wife 4 and is forbidden. Every link in the chain shifts by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'came upon'. Here it means he married her and lived with her.
After the death of.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule underneath both cases is the same: a woman is forbidden only if her sister is still alive and is truly his wife. Changing whether wife 1 is really dead shifts which women in the chain are valid.

phrases.english: And if he came upon the second
after the death of the first,
phrases.notes: Here the report was true: the first wife really had died.

phrases.english: he is permitted to the second and to the fourth,
and they free their co-wives,
and he is forbidden to the third and to the fifth.
